newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks rise at open but underperform Dow.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks rise at open but underperform Dow.

text.p: * Toronto stocks opened a bit higher on Wednesday, trailing Wall Street after it jumped on unexpectedly weak U.S. data. * 8 million shares traded early worth C$92 million.

Toronto's key equities index popped up at Wednesday's open but quickly turned negative, with investors turning their attention to tomorrow's slew of U.S. economic data and the threat of U.S. inflation.
"It certainly turned around," said Fred Ketchen, ScotiaMcLeod's director of equity trading. "The bond market had some early gains and sort of pooped out."

After this morning's unexpectedly soft U.S. data which showed little inflation if any, Ketchen said many market players became concerned about the possible outcome of July consumer prices and other statistics, due out on Thursday.
Nine of 14 sub-indexes dropped. The stronger side, led by conglomerates which soared 1.5 percent, was overwhelmed by falling consumer products, oils and retail.
* Northern Telecom Ltd fell the most, dipping 2.70 to 139.85 in active dealings.
* Seagram Co fell 1 to 48 ahead of its fourth quarter results expected today.
